text:
jamie: Heads-up — we're seeing a burst of correctable ECC on az3a-gpu-pool-12, gnode-712. Perf degraded and a few pods reporting Xid 31.

sara: saw the alert, grabbing GPU logs now. Can we isol ate the instance from serving while we collect nvmetrics?

ops-bot: ALERT: gpu-ecc-spike detected on gnode-712 (az3a). Incident ID: INC-212455. Threshold crossed: 14/min.

leo: tagging for drain. Jamie, can you confirm which queues are on that pool? I want to avoid blocking high-priority realtime routes.

jamie: Realtime routes: inference-realtime-east, fallback to dedicated-eu-west for background jobs. We can shift realtime to az3b for next 15m if we throttle batch jobs.

mike: If we drain gnode-712 we'll lose ~32 concurrent sequence streams. Autoscaler will try to place, but az3a capacity tight — we should pre-warm az3b.

jamie: agreed. Sara — start an isolated drain with cordon + eviction for best-effort. Command: ```kubectl cordon gnode-712 && kubectl drain gnode-712 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```

sara: running drain, grabbing nvme dmesg and nvidia-smi -q. Pasting snippet: ```GPU 0: ECC 48 correctable, 2 uncorrectable; Xid 31 spike; GPU temp normal; pci link flaps intermittent```

leo: that's weird — temps and power normal. Could be card-level memory degradation. RMA likely. Rma-team, can you schedule expedited replacement?

rma-team: we have a spare on the way to us-west; lead time to az3a is ~6h with courier. Next-day via ground is 18h. We can do temporary capacity via az3b/az4 if you want to avoid affecting SLAs.

mike: cost tradeoff: moving traffic cross-AZ bumps egress and spot usage. How bad is perf hitting SLO?

jamie: p90 latency is +120ms on realtime for the affected customers, error rate +0.7%. Not yet a P1 but trending. Recommend: 1) drain and isolate gnode-712 now, 2) place new live instances in az3b and az4 to absorb load, 3) failover high-priority routes to az3b with weighted routing 80/20 for 30 min, 4) RMA hardware and mark gnode-712 as DOA for lifecycle.

leo: I'll kick off weighted routing change in the router: ```routectl set-weight inference-realtime-east az3a=20 az3b=80 --reason "gpu ecc surge"``` — doing a config push in 2min.

ops-bot: NOTE: rolling routing config push scheduled by leo in 2m. Watch for 502s.

sara: drain completed. All inference pods evicted, node cordoned. Dump uploaded to s3://redwood-ops/gpu-dumps/gnode-712/2124554321.tar.gz

jamie: good. Leo, after you shift weights let's keep an eye on cost and throttle batch jobs to prevent preemption. Mike — can you open a quick runbook for cost alert if cross-AZ egress > $X in 1h?

mike: on it. Creating ticket INF-COST-212455 and adding an hourly monitor.

rma-team: booked courier pickup window tomorrow 09:00 local, ETA to az3a 15:00. If you want faster, we can authorize air at +$800.

jamie: let's wait for telemetry 30-60m. If errors keep trending up, authorize air. Leo, confirm routing once done.

leo: routing change done. Initial telemetry: p90 down to +30ms, errors stable. No 502 spike.

sara: uploading post-drain health checks. No kernel oops found, but memtest shows growing single-bit errors on GPU 0 across multiple passes.

jamie: ok final decision: mark gnode-712 for RMA, keep it drained and in maintenance. Keep weighted routing for 1h then slowly ramp back if stable. Close INC-212455 when courier pickup confirmed.

mike: cost monitor in place, rma ticket created, courier pending. I'll annotate billing impact to finance later.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: INC-212455 status=mitigated, node=gnode-712 state=drained, rma_ticket=RMA-4921.

leo: thanks team. Follow-ups: add a health probe for ECC corrected-rate > 10/min to auto-quarantine; create a small playbook for courier vs ground decision matrix.

jamie: noted — I'll draft the playbook and tag ops and sre. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
